questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.**

Surreptitious
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **‘secret’.**

**Surreptitious** means **‘kept secret or stealthy.’**

Hence, **a secret **is the correct answer as it has a very similar meaning to the given word.

Hesitation means ‘the action of pausing before doing something’

Impious means ‘showing a lack of respect for God or religion’

Artless means ‘without guile or deception.’

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/Phrase.**

Adam's ale
questions.solution:
The correct is **‘Water’.**

The idiom **‘Adam’s ale’** means **water**, as a reference to the only drink available to Adam – the first man, according to the Bible.

Hence, Option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

Rohan was upset and so (picked up) his food while his cousins ate heartily.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **‘picked at’.**

The phrasal verb **‘pick at’** means **‘to eat slowly’.**

Hence, it fits the context of the sentence as Rohan was upset and ate his food slowly.

The other options,

Picked out means ‘to choose from something’

Picked on means ‘to bully or single someone out’

Picked up means ‘to lift’.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.**

I will write an essay.

options.text: An essay will have been written by me.
An essay will be written by me.
An essay has been written by me.
An essay had been written by me.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **‘An essay will be written by me.’**

Sentence 1 changes the tense to future perfect and makes the sentence incorrect.

Sentence 3 changes the tense to present perfect and makes the sentence incorrect.

Sentence 4 changes the tense to past perfect and makes the sentence incorrect.

Only **Sentence 2 **correctly preserves the simple future tense and is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/Phrase.**

At one's wit's end
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **‘To get puzzled’.**

The phrase **‘at one’s wit's end’** means **at the end of one’s mental resources; perplexed**.

Hence, Option 3 is the closest meaning of the given phrase and is the correct answer.

An example sentence is: **‘The murder case had the detective at his wit's end’.**

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.**

Neha said, "Need I write a letter?"

options.text: Neha asked if she have to write a letter.
Neha asked if she had been writing a letter.
Neha asked of writing a letter.
Neha asked if she had to write a letter.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **‘Neha asked if she had to write a letter.’**

Sentence 1 is grammtically incorrect due to tense mismatch.

Sentence 2 changes the meaning of the sentence from a question of writing a letter to a question of was the letter being written.

Sentence 3 uses an incorrect pronoun, ‘of’, making the sentence incorrect.

Only **Sentence 4** accurately converts the given Direct speech into reported speech and is the correct answer.

questions.question:

 **Example: **I'd rather turn myself over to *my enemies and be done with it than bring the slightest harm to you.*

• Done in means very tired

 **Example: ***Poor Tom was done in when he got home.*

**The correct sentence is:** **‘***I had not completed my project so I thought I **was done for **when the manager asked me to hand it in.’*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.**

The student asked me if (1)/ I knew that Kalidas was the greater (2)/ than any other poet. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The error is in **part 2** of the sentence

The comparative degree, ‘greater’ does employ the use of the definite article as it is a comparison between two things. Only the superlative degree uses ‘the’ to signify the superiority.

Hence, the correct sentence is:

**‘The student asked me if I knew that Kalidas was greater than any other poet’.**

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P- When the robber was near her bed, she stood up suddenly, 'brandishing the knife.

Q- One night the robber did enter her room but Lakshmi did not make any sound.

R- She just kept a tight hold of the knife and pretended to be sound asleep.

S- The robber was taken aback and with a loud cry, he ran out.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **QRPS.**

Q is the first sentence as it forms the beginning, seen from ‘one night’.

It is followed by R, showing that Lakshmi tightly held the knife.

It is followed by P, showing what happened when the robber was near her bed.

It is followed by S, showing what happened when the robber was shocked.

Thus, the correct combination is QRPS, as seen in **Option 3.**

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of ****labelled**** sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P- They never desert us even when all fair weather friends have deserted us.

Q- Books are never failing friends.

R- They dispel the dark clouds of gloom from our minds and increase our happiness if we are already happy.

S- Through the ages, the scriptures and other great books have provided, immeasurable solace to the wounded and strife-torn humanity.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is **QPRS.**

Q will be the first sentence as it introduces books.

It is followed by P and R which talk about ‘weather’ and how books help.

It is then followed by S, which talks about how books have helped humanity.

Thus, the correct combination is QPRS, as seen in **Option 4.**

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with a blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Mother shall return ________ an hour.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **‘within’**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The word **‘within’** is used to denote the period between the current time and the specified time.

 
 
• Within can be used in the following ways- as a preposition (followed by a noun):
 
 
• **Example: **Can you complete the work within a month?
 
 
 
 
 
• In the context of the sentence, it means that the mother shall return any point of time between the current time and an hour later.

Hence, **‘within’** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.**

Ritika decided to get up early (1)/ to wear a nice dress (2)/ and visit her aunt. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The error is in **part 3** of the sentence.

The use of ‘to’ signifies an action. ‘To visit someone’ means to go see a person.

Thus, the correct sentence is:

**‘Ritika decided to get up early to wear a nice dress and to visit her aunt’. **
